rationale: This is essentially the archived "Solvency Rank Displacement from Capitalized R&D" with the archived retained-earnings-repair leg bolted on — an additive variant rather than a new mechanism — and the stated justification is technically wrong, since cross-sectional ranks of zero-R&D firms do shift when other firms' capitalized values change, so the difference is not "exactly zero" for them.

Industry-demeaning both legs is the single most informative unexplored diagnostic for this archive, since it directly tests whether the entire family of R&D×distress alphas is a biotech-versus-tangible-industry composition bet, and the construction is clean and coherent with the stated sign.

The level-to-change pivot is a genuine information-event distinction from the archived coverage signals, but the change leg is dominated by the year-over-year change in operating cash flow, so the signal risks being an R&D-conditioned cash-flow-momentum/earnings-improvement effect — a well-known anomaly family — and the dlc term adds little.

This is the archived "Knowledge-Capital Leverage Overstatement" with ceq substituted for at, and the claim that ranking "neutralizes the pathologies of small or negative book equity" is false — lt/ceq flips sign discontinuously as equity crosses zero, so firms whose capitalized R&D pushes equity from negative to positive will jump from the bottom to the top of the adjusted rank and dominate the long leg for purely mechanical reasons.

The impairment-trigger conditioner (revenue disappointment against the equity cushion) is economically distinct from the archived debt-service and coverage conditioners, but the embedded NEG(sales growth) main effect points against the well-documented sales/asset-growth anomaly direction, and gdwl/ceq inherits the negative-equity sign flip, so any measured spread will need careful decomposition.

Centering both legs to isolate the pure interaction is the correct methodological response to the archive's rank-product signals mechanically loading on R&D intensity, and it is a decisive diagnostic — though the reviewer should note that the product is symmetric, so the long leg will pool high-R&D/high-coverage firms with low-R&D/low-coverage firms, and unwinsorized z-scores of skewed ratios will make the extremes outlier- and microcap-driven.
